title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors, officers and employees of the Company or its subsidiaries (full time, part time or casual), and contractors and consultants whose terms of engagement require compliance with this Policy.

tiers.name: Director or member of Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Designated Person who is a Director or KMP; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Chair of the Board (or, if unavailable, the Chair of the Audit Committee).

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Designated Person who is Chair of the Board; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: All other Designated Persons
tiers.description: Designated Persons other than Directors/KMP or the Chair; distinguished only for clearance, obtained from the Managing Director or Chief Financial Officer.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence or be influenced by the Designated Person in dealings with the Company or Company securities (e.g. spouse, partner, children, dependants), or a company or other entity the Designated Person can control.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any additional Prohibited Period and may extend the half-year/annual-results or AGM periods (clause 5.3(iv)-(v)); the Company notifies affected Designated Persons of the period. No confidentiality requirement is stated for the existence of an additional period itself (as distinct from a refused Clearance, which must be kept confidential).

rules.detail: Absolute, unwaivable ban on entering finance arrangements using Company securities as collateral via options, warrants, derivatives, futures or other financial products issued by third parties such as banks — squarely covering a bank-written OTC put/call. No Clearance route is available for this item (unlike the short-term/frequency restrictions later in clause 6).
rules.evidence: enter finance arrangements involving the Company's securities as collateral, such as options, warrants, derivatives, futures or any other financial products issued over the Company's securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions

rules.detail: Absolute ban on any arrangement limiting the economic risk of a security holding, expressly extended to securities held beneficially, including under any Company incentive plan, so both unvested and vested holdings are covered with no distinction and no Clearance route.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions in products associated with the Company's securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company (such as hedging arrangements). This restriction also applies to Company securities held beneficially (including, for example, in trust or under any Company incentive plan) on the Designated Person's behalf

rules.detail: Monetisation is not separately named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure using Company securities as collateral for finance is a 'finance arrangement involving the Company's securities as collateral' and is banned outright under the same clause as the derivatives ban.

rules.detail: Both collateralised finance arrangements generally (6(a)) and margin lending specifically (6(c)) are banned outright; no tier or security-state carve-out and no Clearance route.

rules.detail: Unlike the absolute bans in 6(a)-(d), short-term/speculative trading (under 90 days) and being involved in more than one sale within six months are permitted only if Clearance has been obtained.

exemption_authority: The approver listed in clause 5.5.1 (Chair of the Board, Chair of the Audit Committee, or the Managing Director/CFO) may give or refuse Clearance for ordinary trades and for the clause 6 short-term/multiple-sale restrictions, at the Company's discretion and without giving reasons. Clause 6(a)-(d) (collateralised finance arrangements, hedging, margin lending, short selling) are flat prohibitions with no Clearance or waiver mechanism at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter finance arrangements involving the Company's securities as collateral, such as options, warrants, derivatives, futures or any other financial products issued over the Company's securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This clause is squarely on point: a bank-written OTC put/call combined with a loan secured on the shares is precisely a 'finance arrangement involving the Company's securities as collateral' using derivatives 'issued ... by third parties such as banks', an absolute and unwaivable prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This restriction also applies to Company securities held beneficially (including, for example, in trust or under any Company incentive plan) on the Designated Person's behalf.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban is not limited to shares already legally held outright — it expressly extends to unvested or plan-held securities, closing off any argument that pre-vesting shares could be hedged.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless a Clearance has been obtained, Designated Persons ... [engage in short-term or speculative trading; multiple sales] — contrasted with items (a)-(d) which carry no such 'unless Clearance obtained' qualifier.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The drafting contrast confirms the finance-arrangement, hedging, margin-lending and short-selling bans cannot be cleared or approved by any officer of the Company, unlike the short-term trading restriction.

summary: A funded collar cannot be implemented under this policy. Clause 6(a) expressly and without any clearance route prohibits Designated Persons and their Connected Persons from entering 'finance arrangements involving the Company's securities as collateral, such as options, warrants, derivatives, futures or any other financial products issued over the Company's securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions' — language that captures precisely a bank-written put/call collar secured by a loan over the shares. Clause 6(b) separately and absolutely bans any hedging arrangement that limits the economic risk of a security holding, extending even to securities held beneficially under a Company incentive plan, and clause 6(c) separately bans dealing pursuant to any margin lending arrangement; none of these three bans can be cleared, waived or approved by any officer of the Company. Ordinary share trading otherwise proceeds under a written Clearance regime (Chair of the Board/Audit Committee, or the Managing Director/CFO, each Clearance valid 3 business days and refusals kept confidential) subject to Prohibited Periods and a 90-day/one-sale-per-six-months short-term trading limit that can itself be cleared. Overall, this is one of the strictest policies reviewed: the funded collar structure is squarely and permanently prohibited, not merely restricted.
